newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel, Lagardere face tight fight for Thomson.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel, Lagardere face tight fight for Thomson.

text.p: French engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom and defence equipment group Lagardere face a close fight for state electronics firm Thomson-CSF but Lagardere may still have the edge, analysts say.

The government relaunched the sale on Wednesday of its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF through a private sale, saying it wanted to create an "industrial electronics and defence (group) able to compete on the international stage".

In the first privatisation attempt last October to prepare the defence electronics business for restructuring of the European defence industry, the government said it preferred Lagardere's proposal to Alcatel's offer.

But the proposed sale of the whole Thomson group was scrapped in December after the privatisation commission objected to Lagardere's plans to sell Thomson Multimedia, Thomson's money-losing consumer electronics arm, to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics. Now the government will sell Thomson Multimedia separately.
Lagardere is expected to renew its bid in competition with Alcatel which has lined up France's two aircraft companies, state-owned Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation , to boost its chances.
Investors gave their own verdict on the outcome, driving down Lagardere shares 2.69 percent to 162.50 francs ($28.41). "The market is betting on Alcatel," said a trader.
Alcatel's shares shed 0.68 percent to 585 francs in line with the market. But analysts said nothing was certain.

Lehman Brothers analyst Charles Armitage said Alcatel's prospects looked stronger this time but it was hard to predict the result. "They (the government) may want to say their original decision was right and save face," he said.
The centre-right government said last year it liked Lagardere's offer on the grounds of "industrial logic".
Lagardere said confidently on Wednesday the government's statement "practically confirmed all elements of the project we presented last year and which won us victory over our rival".
Meanwhile, Alcatel insisted on the "great synergy" between its technologies and those of Thomson-CSF.

Analysts said Alcatel had boosted its credibility enormously in lining up Aerospatiale and Dassault to mount a joint bid for Thomson-CSF. "They bring to Alcatel the credibility in the defence market which it lacked in its original bid," one said.
The aligning of this trio with Thomson CSF would create a huge vertically integrated defence group making everything from electronics components to weapons systems and jet fighters.

But this may not be what the government wants, some analysts said. "If they said they wanted to create a defence and aerospace pole, Alcatel would be the ultimate compromise," one said. "The fact they said defence electronics pole, I see as giving Lagardere the edge."
CDC Bourse analyst Gilbert Ferrand said the goverment was "putting the emphasis on the electronics defence pole which is the plan proposed by Lagardere".
Analysts said the government's statement welcoming interest from European groups also could favour Lagardere and its allies.
Lagardere had proposed merging its missiles business, 50 percent held by British Aerospace , with Thomson-CSF. Lagardere also has a British partner in its Matra Marconi satellite business, GEC Plc .

From an industrial viewpoint, an eventual joining up of Thomson's operations with those of GEC-Marconi would not only bring major savings but also create a group with $11 billion in sales able to take on such U.S. heavyweights as Lockheed Martin and Raytheon .

Another analyst, however, said he believed Alcatel was now the favourite but that the government wanted to bring Lagardere on board. Prime Minister Alain Juppe was reported by a French newspaper to have met the chairmen of Lagardere and Alcatel last week and tried to get them both involved.
"What they are trying to do is get both Alcatel and Matra (Lagardere) aboard," said Peter Lewis of Jane's Defence Weekly. "But that will be hard with all the bad blood between the two."
"If it (Lagardere) wants to come in alongside Alcatel, the government will be only too happy," said Lewis. "Otherwise they will give it to Alcatel-Aerospatiale-Dassault."
Other analysts also suggested the wording of the government statement left the door open to an alliance between the two.
"That would be the ultimate all-French solution," said one. ($ = 5.718 French Francs)
